question: A 23-year-old female college basketball player presents in Sports Clinic after she felt a "pop" in her knee after coming down with a rebound. To examine the patient, you have her lie down on the table with her knees flexed 90 degrees. With your hand around her knee you are able to draw the tibia toward you from underneath the femur. The torn structure implicated by this physical exam maneuver has which of the following attachments?

options.opa: The posterior intercondylar area of tibia and the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femur
options.opb: The anterior intercondylar area of tibia and the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femur
options.opd: The lateral epicondyle of the femur and the head of fibula
options.ope: The medial condyle of the femur and the medial condyle of the tibia

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "23-year-old female athlete" -> "felt a 'pop' in the knee" -> "mechanism suggests possible ligament injury" -> "physical exam shows tibia can be drawn forward" -> "indicates anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury" -> "ACL attaches to the anterior intercondylar area of tibia" -> "and the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femur" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Knee injury with 'pop' sound" -> "suggests acute ligamentous injury" -> "anterior drawer test shows tibial translation" -> "indicates involvement of the ACL" -> "ACL connects anterior intercondylar area of tibia" -> "to the lateral femur" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Athlete with knee instability" -> "positive anterior drawer test" -> "suggests ACL tear" -> "ACL originates from anterior intercondylar area of tibia" -> "and attaches to the lateral femur" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Knee examination reveals tibial movement" -> "indicates possible ACL injury" -> "ACL has specific attachments" -> "anterior intercondylar area of tibia" -> "and posteromedial aspect of lateral femur" -> 75%
analysis: The physical exam maneuver described suggests an anterior drawer test, which indicates a potential tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). The ACL attaches from the anterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femur. Therefore, the correct option is the one that describes these attachments.
